(c) Fees. Fees, rates and charges for the collection services outlined in this article shall be as determined by the mayor and council and on file in the office of the clerk. Every residence, business establishment or service agency within the limits of the city and to which garbage and solid waste collection and disposal services are available shall pay a fee for the availability of such service, regardless of whether the residence, business or agency used the service, and based upon a fee schedule approved by the mayor and council. For the purposes of this chapter, the principal occupant or head of household in physical possession of a resident through ownership or lease shall be responsible for payment of the fee. If an account exists with the city of services, the fee shall be added to and denominated separately on monthly account statements.
(d) Night collection. Should the best interest of the public be served by collection of refuse from certain areas in the city at night, the city shall make such collections. The occupants of all residences or places of business within the designated area shall be notified of the hours of such collection. All persons so notified shall comply with such order and shall place the containers as designated within such hours.
(e) Landlord's responsibility. All garbage charges to a complex of apartments, houses, mobile homes or businesses will be billed to the landlord of the property, and the landlord shall be responsible to the city for payment of assessed charges.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. I, § 3, 10-6-1998)
404:
No person shall engage in the business of and receive compensation for the collection or disposal of garbage or solid waste within the city except pursuant to a contractual agreement approved by the mayor and council and duly executed by all parties thereto and under terms and conditions set out in the contractual agreement or in this Code, unless otherwise explicitly stated herein. It further shall be unlawful for any person to collect refuse within the city except from his own residence, business, service agency or industrial plant, without first having obtained a proper permit from the state department of natural resources and the city, and without first having paid an occupational tax or regulatory fee, as applicable.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. I, § 4, 10-6-1998)
405:
Every person in possession, charge or control of any building from which business trash, industrial waste or other waste is accumulated or produced shall be required to provide and keep in a suitable place, readily accessible to city crews or other licensed and authorized private collectors, authorized public receptacles and containers suitable for the storage of all such waste materials which will normally accumulate between the established collection dates. The city manager or designee shall determine the quantity and location of such receptacles and shall determine whether such receptacles and containers are in a serviceable condition.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. I, § 5, 10-6-1998)
406:
All public and private receptacles and containers shall be of safe construction and design and shall be maintained in good, orderly and serviceable condition at all times. The user shall promptly replace any receptacle or container, which does not conform or which has ragged or sharp edges or any other defects likely to hamper or injure the person collecting the contents therefrom or the public generally. If such container, after appropriate notice, has not been replaced, the city manager or designee shall have the right to suspend further collection of such waste material until such time as the container is brought into compliance.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. I, § 6, 10-6-1998)
409:
The city manager or designee shall investigate complaints or violations of any provisions of this chapter. They shall determine if there has been a violation, issue warnings and initiate an attempt to obtain compliance with this chapter by the person in violation thereof.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. II, § 1, 10-6-1998)
410:
The city manager or designee shall be authorized to sign a complaint or issue a summons against a violator of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. II, § 2, 10-6-1998)
411:
In case of any violation of this chapter, the city manager or designee, and the city attorney in addition to any other remedies, may institute injunction, mandates or other appropriate proceedings to prevent such violation, to correct or abate such violation.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. II, § 3, 10-6-1998)
412:
Upon appropriate notice to the person violating this chapter, the city manager or designee may suspend any service or the use of any facility maintained by the city during the period such violation continues to exist.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. II, § 4, 10-6-1998)
413:
Any person violating this chapter may be held liable for damages, and the recovery shall be in a sum of not less than $110.00, nor more than $550.00 for each violation. The city attorney may institute a proceeding in any court having jurisdiction thereof to collect such civil penalty. If the violation has been committed by the owner of the property on which the violation occurs, the clerk may further proceed to collect the costs to the city of eliminating, removing or cleaning the premises in the same manner as provided by law for tax executions.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. II, § 5, 10-6-1998)
416:
The practices and procedures specified in this chapter shall be employed by persons in the city in order to facilitate the collection of solid wastes.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 1, 10-6-1998)
417:
All refuse shall be placed and maintained in containers as specified in this chapter. All containers shall be maintained at all times with tight-fitting lids or covers. All garage placed in containers for collection shall first be drained of all liquids, and shall be wrapped, bagged, or enclosed in paper or plastic material.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 2, 10-6-1998)
418:
All household trash shall be drained of all liquids prior to its being placed in refuse receptacles. Household trash may be combined with garbage.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 3, 10-6-1998)
419:
All waste materials of an injurious nature, such as broken glass, light bulbs, sharp pieces of metal, fluorescent tubes and television tubes shall be securely packaged or wrapped (used needles shall be placed in hard plastic container with lid) for the purpose of preventing injury to the collection crews or third parties.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 4, 10-6-1998)
420:
No hazardous refuse or building materials shall be placed in any receptacle at any time. The city shall not be required to collect any hazardous refuse or building material. All hazardous refuse shall be secured against the possibility of causing injury to any person and shall not be placed on public property or private property without the written consent of the owner thereof.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 5, 10-6-1998)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, ch. 10; environment, ch. 22.
421:
No residence or business shall place for collection at one time more than five cubic yards or 400 pounds of trash. If the residence or business establishment places trash for collection which exceeds these limits, the residence or business shall be assessed an additional fee in an amount based on the actual cost of equipment, labor, transport or hauling and tippage fees needed for collection and disposal.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 6, 10-6-1998)
422:
All persons, firms, businesses, institutions or corporations utilizing city pickup of trash at a place of trade or business shall be required to break down any and all boxes, whether made of cardboard, wood, or other material, before placing the boxes into collection bins, receptacles, or other designated and approved collection points. To break down a box, it shall be rendered into a flat shape by whatever means necessary so that it no longer retains its three-dimensional shape and utilizes as little space as possible. Failure to break down boxes shall result in a violation of this chapter or the refusal by city sanitation officials to remove the garbage, or both.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 7, 10-6-1998)
423:
(a) It shall be prohibited to place or mix yard trimmings with municipal solid waste within the city. Yard trimmings shall not be disposed at any municipal solid waste disposal facility having a linear and leachate collection system or requiring vertical expansion located within the city. Yard trimmings and small branches shall be sorted in the following manner.
(b) All leaves, clippings and small branches shall be collected and stored in lawn and garden bags no larger than 40 gallons in capacity. All such leaves and trimmings stored in bags shall be placed at the edge of the pavement of any public right-of-way used for road purposes.
(1) All limbs shall be cut into lengths of no more than four feet each and shall be neatly stacked in piles not to exceed an area of four feet by four feet at or near the curb to facilitate easy collection by the city.
(c) If any residence or business establishment places yard trimmings for collection that exceeds these limits, the residence or business shall be assessed an additional fee in the amount based on the actual cost of equipment, labor and tippage fees needed for collection. The city will not pick up yard waste mixed with other debris. Trash other than yard waste must be in a separate stack.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 8, 10-6-1998; Ord. No. 08-43, 4-1-2008)
424:
The owner of property on which trees are cut down, whether by the owner or another, is required to remove promptly following the cutting at the owner's expense all tree trunks, logs, limbs, tops or other debris resulting therefrom, when such materials are clearly visible from any public street, alley, sidewalk, lane or path from the property of another that adjoins the property on which the materials are located. Such materials shall not be destroyed or removed by burning.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 9, 10-6-1998)
425:
All individuals, firms, businesses, partnerships, proprietorships or corporations engaged in the business of yard maintenance, landscaping, nursery operation or in the business of trimming or removing trees, shrubbery, or similar growth, who shall contract with the property owner, the owner's agent or occupant to perform services on the property shall remove from the property all sawdust, branches, stumps and all portions of the byproducts of the services performed, as well as all rubbish associated therewith including rocks, concrete, dirt and trimmings.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 10, 10-6-1998)
426:
It shall be unlawful for any firm, partnership, proprietorship or corporation to trim trees or bushes, do landscaping or yard work for compensation within the city unless the byproduct from those services is immediately removed from the premises and placed or deposited by the contractor in the city designated landfill or hauling station, or unless arrangements are made by the contractor or property owner for yard trimmings removal by the city for a fee. Compensation shall be interpreted to include receiving as compensation the wood, limbs and other residue from such trimming and cutting. Any form of compensation shall place the burden of disposal directly upon the individual or contractor performing the task.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 11, 10-6-1998)
427:
Upon request, the city may, where such service is found to be economical and in the best interest of the general health, safety and welfare, collect, or, arrange for the collection, of normal household furniture and appliances, including sofas, chairs, beds, refrigerators, washers, dryers, hot water heaters and similar items, but not including furnaces. Persons requesting this service shall notify the office of the city manager or designee as to the date the collection will occur. The city shall have the right to set and collect a fee for this service.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 12, 10-6-1998)
428:
The following activities are declared to be unlawful and in violation of this chapter:
(1) Public streets and private property. No person shall place any accumulations of refuse, trash, or litter in any street, sidewalk, median strip, alley or other public right of way, nor upon any private property, except with the written consent thereof and then only in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.
(2) Blockage of drainage. At no time shall trash be placed in a manner to obstruct drains, utility meters, walkways or streets. It shall be unlawful to use brooms, rakes, blowers or other sweeping, raking or debris removal tools or equipment to sweep, rake, blow or otherwise deposit or accumulate trash, garbage, gardening residue, clippings, limbs, ashes, alluvium, sediment, litter or other debris of any kind in or on city streets, walkways, drains, pipes or gutters. It shall be unlawful to place, accumulate or otherwise deposit any type of the aforementioned debris or material into a city drain, pipe, gutter or other draining conduit or receptacle.
(3) Unauthorized storage. Any accumulation of refuse or trash items, or any litter, on any lot, property, premises, public streets, alley or other public or private place not permitted by this chapter, is declared to be a nuisance. Failure of owner or occupant to remove and correct any such accumulation of refuse after appropriate notice from the city manager or designee shall raise the presumption that such person intended to violate this chapter.
(4) Junk. It shall be unlawful for any person to place or leave outside any building or dwelling, except as specified in section 38-92, any dilapidated furniture, appliance, machinery, equipment, building material, junked motor vehicle, tires or other items which are either in a partially used, wrecked, junked, dismantled or inoperative condition, and which are not completely enclosed within a building or dwelling.
(5) Sweeping and blowing. It shall be unlawful to sweep or blow with a blower, grass clippings, leaves and other debris onto a city sidewalk, gutter or street.
(6) Dumping. It shall be unlawful and in violation of this section to dump, place or leave bricks, blocks, rocks, lumber, asphalt, cement, concrete, concrete products or waste, roofing, sheetrock, leaves, limbs, bushes, trees, roots, dead animals, appliances, equipment, bed springs, mattresses, furniture, fixture, motors, engines, chemical wastes, industrial or commercial waste or rubbish, scrap metal, fence wire, vehicles or parts thereof, tires, building materials or supplies, and inorganic solid material of any type or kind except as authorized herein.
(7) Fires. It shall be unlawful and in violation of this chapter to set any fire to any solid waste, litter or rubbish, or to allow a fire to burn inside or outside of an authorized receptacle, or in any other way attempt to damage or destroy the garbage and solid waste collection containers provided by the city.
(8) Container of another. It shall be unlawful and in violation of this chapter for any person to dump, place or leave any item at a garbage and solid waste collection area or in any collection container unless such person has permission of the owner and/or occupant of the premises on which the area or container is located and such arrangement is authorized by the city manager or designee.
(9) Billboards.
a. It shall be unlawful for owners to fail to maintain billboards in a manner that prevents loose paper, bills and other litter and debris resulting from the use of such signs and billboards. The owners or their agents immediately upon accumulation shall remove any such debris, loose papers, bills and other litter.
b. Any such item or items, which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of 30 days after notice of violation, shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject to being removed from the property by the city without further notice. The city may charge the owner or occupant a fee for the cost of removing such item or items, and may collect the fees for removal as prescribed herein. This section shall not apply to licensed junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning, or salvaging of equipment or furniture.
(10) Scavenging. No person other than the owner thereof or an agent or employee of the city manager or designee shall disturb or interfere with any container used for the purpose of storing refuse pending its collection, remove any contents therefrom, or remove such container from its collection place.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 13, 10-6-1998)
429:
Any such item or items, which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of 30 days after notice of violation of this chapter, shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject to being removed from the property by the city without further notice. The city may charge the owner or occupant a fee for the cost of removing such item or items. The clerk may collect any unpaid charge for removal in the same manner as delinquent taxes. This section shall not apply to licensed junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning, or salvaging of equipment or furniture.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. III, § 14, 10-6-1998)
432:
All commercial establishments shall store their refuse in containers, as specified in this chapter, to eliminate wind-driven debris and unsightly litter in and about their establishments. Approved methods of containerization shall include refuse receptacles, bulk containers and detachable containers. Such establishment shall immediately clean up any spillage or overflow.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. IV, § 1, 10-6-1998)
433:
All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash. The owner or occupant of the commercial establishment shall place a sufficient number of containers in such area to maintain a clean, neat and sanitary condition at all times. The number of such containers to be placed in service for a particular establishment shall be set by the city manager or designee. The occupant of the premises shall maintain surveillance to ensure that all litter is placed in the proper container and the area is kept clean. The city manager or designee may require refuse receptacles to be screened or buffered or moved if it can be feasibly determined that a loading or unloading area is inadequate, unsanitary or unsightly. If the occupant violates this section where all other remedies have failed, collection service, and at the discretion of the city water service may be suspended until such time as the owner or occupant of the premises brings such premises into full compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. IV, § 2, 10-6-1998)
434:
All construction and demolition contractors shall provide on-site refuse receptacles, bulk containers or detachable containers for loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials and other trash (no hazardous waste shall be deposited in the containers) produced by those working at the construction site. A separate container shall be provided for metal scraps free of all other debris at the construction site. The site shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number of refuse receptacles (not to exceed four bulk containers, or detachable containers), shall be determined by the size of the job. The designated collection contractor upon completion of the construction shall remove dirt, mud, construction materials or other debris upon any public or private property belonging to a person other than the owner of the construction site.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. IV, § 3, 10-6-1998)
437:
Residential garbage collection shall be provided as follows:
(1) Garbage and solid waste at residences within the city shall be collected only by departments and employees of the city, or pursuant to a contract or franchise issued by the city. Removal by persons for hire or compensation is prohibited.
(2) Collections from residential premises shall be made once weekly, with the exception of holidays or in times when such collection is impossible, such as in the event of natural disasters.
(3) Residents shall place garbage for curbside pickup in carts provided by the city. On the evening before each day assigned by the city sanitation department, or its contractor, for collection in the resident's area, the cart will be placed at a curbside point designated by the city sanitation department no earlier than 6:00 p.m. for pick up the next day. The cart will be removed from the curbside point by the resident no later than 8:00 a.m. on the day after the assigned collection date. Failure to remove a cart by 8:00 a.m. on the day after the assigned collection date shall result in a fine of $10.00 per day until the cart is removed. At other times, carts will be stored by the residents where possible in locations not visible from the street or road on which the garage is collected.
(4) The city shall initially provide and bear the cost of the first cart for each residence. In the event the cart is insufficient to contain the garbage for a residence, the resident shall bear the cost of placement of an additional cart at the residence. In the event a cart is lost, stolen or abused, the resident shall bear the cost of placement of another cart at the residence.
(5) In the event the cart is not used for a period of three weeks, then the cart shall be removed from the residence.
(6) Persons having physical handicaps, which prevent them from placing carts at curbsides, shall be exempted from the requirement to place the cart at the curbside. The other requirements for collection and disposal of garbage contained within this chapter will nonetheless apply to persons exempted under this subsection.
(7) Persons required to maintain containers under this chapter shall maintain the containers in a sanitary condition, tightly covered at all times other than filling, emptying and cleaning, and free from odor. Such containers shall be filled in such a manner as to allow pickup by one person, except when hoist type containers are used. Such containers shall be further maintained to prevent the overflow and scattering of trash, garbage, refuse, other solid waste, or water/rainwater.
(8) All apartment buildings or structures containing in excess of six dwelling units are required to use hoist type dumpsters or containers that are compatible for loading by mechanical means by garbage and solid waste collection vehicles maintained by the city sanitation department for the accumulation of garbage by building or structure residents. In apartment buildings or structures containing less than six dwelling units, each occupied dwelling unit, household or apartment within the city shall provide at least one container and shall provide additional containers as required by the city sanitation department.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. V, § 1, 10-6-1998)
438:
Garbage collection at commercial establishments shall be provided as follows:
(1) Commercial garbage and solid waste shall be collected and disposed pursuant to a contractual agreement entered into by a private garbage and solid waste collection and disposal service and the city, as evidenced by a written agreement approved by the mayor and council. A copy of such contractual agreement shall remain in the office of the clerk and be available for inspection by members of the public during the clerk's regular office hours.
(2) Collections from businesses and commercial enterprises within the city shall be at times as established by the mayor and council and set out in the contractual agreement with the private garbage and solid waste disposal referenced in subsection (1) of this section.
(3) Service to commercial establishments will be provided by a schedule that is provided by the sanitation superintendent. Such collections shall be limited to a maximum of two refuse receptacles per collection or the standard bulk container to be collected by a private contractual agency, as contemplated by subsection (1) of this section.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. V, § 2, 10-6-1998)
439:
Industrial waste shall be collected, removed and disposed of by any factory, plant or enterprise creating or causing such waste.
(Ord. No. 99-05B, art. V, § 3, 10-6-1998)
